mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates indicate tighter monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a strong labor market, which is positive for corporate earnings and thus for S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of periods following a UNRATE drop below 4%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in real final sales (RSAFS) above 2% indicates strong consumer demand, which is positive for corporate revenues and thus for S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of periods when RSAFS growth exceeds 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 0.5% over three months signals increased economic activity, which is positive for S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO growth exceeds 0.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment (UNRATE) and rising employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which is positive for consumer spending and thus for S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of periods when UNRATE is below 5% and PAYEMS is rising, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of GDP growth (GDPC1) and CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals economic expansion with inflationary pressures, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days if inflation exceeds growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL growth exceeds GDPC1 growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, rising federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) increase borrowing costs and reduce corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust economic activity, which is positive for S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when both INDPRO and HOUST are growing, the hypothesis is rejected.
